meta.title: Two Compilers, One Assembly
meta.subtitle: Burst does not speed your code up — it compiles a different language that happens to be spelled like C#, and the way back is a function pointer

views.label: The attribute has to be on both
views.note: On the method and on the containing type. An analyzer warns when you miss the type — and deliberately stays quiet for system structs.

views.label: Ahead of time, not just in time
views.note: One intermediate form, two compilers. One emits managed code with a collector under it; the other emits machine code with none.

views.label: The only doorway back
views.note: Native code cannot call a managed method. It calls an address, parked in a static that both worlds agree on, that happens to point at one.

views.label: What crossing costs
views.note: Every crossing is an indirect call plus a marshalling boundary, and everything on the far side runs at interpreted-plus-jit speed.

cards.title: The package is a shim now
items: The Burst package is version 2.0.0 · Burst package, package.json:4
Its entire runtime folder is one file of type forwarders · Burst package, Runtime/TypeForwarders.cs
The compiler, the attribute, and the intrinsics all live in the editor now
So there is no Burst source to read in the project — only what calls it

cards.title: The attribute pair, and the exemption
items: Marking the method but not the containing type raises warning EA0010 · Diagnostics.cs:72
The message names the fix: add the attribute to the type as well · Diagnostics.cs:73
The analyzer returns without warning for anything implementing the system interface · BurstCompilerAnalyzer.cs:65
So the one case the handbook warns you about is exactly the case that stays silent

cards.title: How the doorway is actually built
items: A method marked discard has no body in the native build · ECBInterop.interop.gen.cs:26
Calling it and seeing nothing happen is how the code detects it is native
The managed address is parked in a shared static both worlds read · ECBInterop.interop.gen.cs:55
And handed over by marshalling a delegate to a function pointer · ECBInterop.interop.gen.cs:71

cards.title: Where this shows up in real code
items: Every managed command handler in the command buffer is marked discard · ECBInterop.cs:50
The reverse direction compiles a managed delegate into native · ECBInterop.interop.gen.cs:67
Playback checks a per-chain flag and picks the native or managed walker · EntityCommandBufferPlayback.cs:321
The entity id table itself is a shared static for the same reason · EntityComponentStoreEntities.cs:22
